## Description {#details}

The µTest++ framework provides a set of literal operators and wrappers to facilitate the creation of strongly typed operands within test expressions. These features enable developers to write clear and type-safe comparisons, improving both readability and correctness in test cases.

Literal operators, available in the dedicated <code>literals</code> namespace, allow constants to be expressed with explicit types, such as integers and floating-point values. For dynamic values, wrappers are provided to convert them into recognised types at run-time.

This approach ensures that both compile-time constants and run-time values can be compared accurately and expressively, supporting robust and maintainable test code.


<SectionUser title="Examples">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::to&#95;i &#123;answer&#125; == 42<Link to="#ga1613ccf081248c601bed0f3022fba652">&#95;i</Link>);</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (mt::to&#95;f &#123;expression&#125; == 42<Link to="#gadcff4454bf86ea03c0c3d1be42b04e12">&#95;f</Link>);</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>

<SectionDefinition>

## Deprecated Type Wrappers


Strongly-typed wrappers for explicit type conversion.

These type aliases provide wrappers for converting values and expressions to specific types for use with µTest++ comparators and test expressions.

The <code><Link to="#ga1613ccf081248c601bed0f3022fba652">&#95;i</Link></code>, <code><Link to="#ga2e2ad62d8c5d6e3abcfca9a897ae61de">&#95;u8</Link></code>, etc. forms are now deprecated as of version 3.2.0. Please use the preferred <code>to&#95;&#42;</code> type wrappers for new code, as they offer improved clarity and consistency.


<SectionUser title="Deprecated">
Use the corresponding <code>to&#95;&#42;</code> type wrappers instead (since 3.2.0).
</SectionUser>

<SectionDefinition>

## Type Wrappers


Strongly-typed wrappers for converting dynamic values and expressions to specific types recognised by µTest++ comparators.

These type aliases provide a modern, type-safe mechanism for explicitly converting values to the required types for µTest++ test expressions and comparators. Each alias is a wrapper around <code><Link to="/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/type-traits/value">type&#95;traits::value</Link>&lt;T&gt;</code>, ensuring that the value is treated as the specified type within the framework.

The <code>to&#95;&#42;</code> forms are the preferred approach since version 3.2.0, superseding the older <code><Link to="#ga1613ccf081248c601bed0f3022fba652">&#95;i</Link></code>, <code><Link to="#ga2e2ad62d8c5d6e3abcfca9a897ae61de">&#95;u8</Link></code>, etc. aliases, which are now deprecated.


<SectionUser title="Example">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing>

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="keywordtype">int</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"> x = 42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight><Highlight kind="keyword">auto</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"> wrapped = <Link to="#gab6ddb21470182cbdcf06436cde43718f">to&#95;i</Link>&#123;x&#125;; </Highlight><Highlight kind="comment">// Explicitly treat x as an int for test</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">comparison</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>


<SectionUser title="Since">
3.2.0
</SectionUser>

### operator&quot;&quot;&#95;b() {#gaa2bfc74376f8c110053bfa6e06e40772}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>auto micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::literals::operator&quot;&quot;&#95;b (const char &#42; name, decltype(sizeof(&quot;&quot;)) size)</>}
  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
User-defined literal operator to convert to <code>bool</code>.

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="name">Pointer to the character sequence representing the literal.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="size">The size of the character sequence.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
An instance of a wrapper type convertible to <code>bool</code> and supporting equality comparisons.
</SectionUser>

This user-defined literal operator enables the creation of strongly-typed boolean constants from character sequences at compile time.

The operator is particularly useful in test expressions, allowing string literals to be suffixed with <code><Link to="#ga74e6e2bffc2fc2dea47f979b5b55ea64">&#95;b</Link></code> (for example, <code>&quot;feature&#95;enabled&quot;<Link to="#ga74e6e2bffc2fc2dea47f979b5b55ea64">&#95;b</Link></code>) to produce a type-safe value that integrates seamlessly with the µTest++ comparators and reporting mechanisms.

The returned type is a lightweight wrapper that behaves as a <code>bool</code> and supports equality comparison with both other named instances and boolean values.


:::info
This operator is intended to facilitate expressive and type-safe test conditions.
:::

</MemberDefinition>

The operator is particularly useful in test expressions, allowing constants to be suffixed with <code><Link to="#gabd2f8b7401162835cb4735e4a7532c36">&#95;c</Link></code> (for example, <code>&#39;A&#39;<Link to="#gabd2f8b7401162835cb4735e4a7532c36">&#95;c</Link></code>) to produce a type-safe value that integrates seamlessly with the µTest++ comparators and reporting mechanisms.

This user-defined literal operator enables the creation of strongly-typed integral constants of type <code>uint8&#95;t</code> from character sequences at compile time.

The operator is particularly useful in test expressions, allowing constants to be suffixed with <code><Link to="#ga2e2ad62d8c5d6e3abcfca9a897ae61de">&#95;u8</Link></code> (for example, <code>255<Link to="#ga2e2ad62d8c5d6e3abcfca9a897ae61de">&#95;u8</Link></code>) to produce a type-safe value that integrates seamlessly with the µTest++ comparators and reporting mechanisms.
